aperture.classification: Declared virtual zero-thickness aperture. No measured pore size, collision diameter or Knudsen-number qualification.

settings.scope: Static ideal-gas collisionless aperture limit, with independently integrated Maxwell moments, complete source energy, source-Cp interval extrema and entropy decomposition. No claim that a real brick or the previous full-pressure cycle is in this regime.

facts: Equilibrium gas unaffected by a small aperture; no collisions during passage.
Final outgoing particle flux is number density times mean speed divided by four.
Velocity-weighted outgoing distribution contains an extra speed factor.
sources.visual_review: PDF page 3 rendered and inspected. First two Maxwell exponents omit the factor 2 in the denominator, whereas the later Cartesian integral and bottom speed distribution include 2. Final stated flux agrees with the normalized Maxwell distribution. We independently integrate the normalized distribution; do not copy the inconsistent exponent.

sources.use: Same gas Cp, formation enthalpy and entropy as existing conditional reactive model. Historical source R is retained for internal thermochemical consistency; no new uncertainty claim.

derived_not_quoted: Outgoing translational energy = 2RT from independent Maxwell speed moments. With internal modes in equilibrium and independent of translational velocity, carried total energy is h-RT/2.
Net flux is difference of both incident fluxes. Total reservoir entropy change follows dS=(dU-sum(mu dn))/T.
Cp-R/2 positive on the selected source interval establishes monotonic carried energy for the stated entropy decomposition.
unknown: Actual pore geometry and collision regime
Connection to a calibrated continuous-to-molecular porous-medium law

affinity.gas_constant_policy: Use the historical USGS book R for this separate source consistency calculation; do not replace any other module R.

verification.rounding_policy: Printed half-last-unit intervals propagated through the linear Cp integrals, Href and Sref. Formation G and logK table comparison retains its own half-last-unit interval. These are arithmetic envelopes, not physical uncertainty. No post-comparison budget fitting.

source.title: Thermodynamic Properties of Minerals and Related Substances at 298.15 K and 1 Bar (10^5 Pascals) Pressure and at Higher Temperatures
source.entropy_reference_policy: Use the 298.15 K row of each individual high-temperature table (two decimal places). Keep the one-decimal summary values in the old facts unchanged.
source.rounding_policy: Each nonblank printed decimal or scientific-notation number carries half its last printed unit for arithmetic consistency comparisons only. Omitted Cp terms remain exact zero terms of the printed nominal formula. This is not physical uncertainty.
unknowns: High-temperature physical fit uncertainty and covariance
Target brick phase amounts and reaction rates
Solid pressure-volume correction away from the stated 1 bar
Nonideal CO2 fugacity and transport limitations

reference_state.reference: Elements in their standard states at 1 bar and stated temperature for formation columns; h(T) storage coordinate must use hf(298.15)+sensible increment, not hf(T) alone.
reference_state.gas_constant_policy: Historical book constant retained as source metadata, never silently replaces runtime modern R.

cp_equation.derivation_classification: exact analytic integral of supplied nominal polynomial; no fitting or coefficient adjustment

uncertainty.method_summary: The book assigns estimated uncertainties; its convention for calorimetric measurements is twice the standard deviation of the mean. Individual upstream uncertainty derivations and cross-species covariance have not been reconstructed.
uncertainty.printed_zero_uncertainty_note: Printed 0.0 is retained at its displayed precision, not interpreted as physically exact.

species.molar_mass_note: Original printed formula weight in grams per mole; historical 1985 atomic weights; no mass uncertainty supplied.

cp.blank_cells_interpretation: Blank cells are omitted terms in the printed polynomial, represented explicitly as zero only in coefficients_nominal; not missing material values filled with zero.

species.check_point_definition: enthalpy_function_j_mol_k is (H(T)-H(298.15 K))/T, not H(T)-H(298.15 K) and not formation enthalpy at T.

interpretation_guards: Only selected original facts are transcribed; no source pages or full PDF included in tracked artifact.
Formation columns at high T use elements at that T; they are not single-species storage enthalpy curves.
Molar volumes apply at 298.15 K and 1 bar; no temperature-independent high-T law or density error envelope is inferred.
Cp source coefficients and independently printed temperature rows remain distinct and may differ because of printed precision or other source inconsistency; derived checks never rewrite either.
No Shomate fitting, no MIA3 raw-sludge properties, no reaction rate or firing recipe.

nitrogen_source.visual_review: Both source PDF pages rendered and inspected; no digest operation.
nitrogen_source.zero_coefficient_policy: Omitted A4 is the exact absent term of the nominal source equation.
nitrogen_source.formation_reference_policy: Nitrogen is the elemental reference state; zero formation enthalpy at Tref does not make h(T) zero.
nitrogen_source.printing_policy: Half-last printed units for source arithmetic only; no measured uncertainty inferred.
